parts.title: Campus Conversation: Joining the Campus Gym
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the campus gym.
Student
Hi, I'd like to join the gym. Do students get a special price?
Staff
Yes. A student membership is twenty dollars a month. You just need to show your student card.
Student
That's cheaper than I thought. What is included in the price?
Staff
You can use the weight room, the swimming pool, and the exercise machines. Fitness classes cost extra, though.
Student
Oh, I wanted to try a yoga class. How much is it?
Staff
Each class is five dollars. But if you buy a ten-class card, you pay only forty dollars.
Student
That sounds like a good deal. When is the gym open? I have classes until four every day.
Staff
We open at six in the morning and close at ten at night, so you can come after your classes.
Student
Perfect. Do I need to bring a towel?
Staff
Yes, please bring your own towel. We sell them here, but they are expensive.
Student
I'll bring one from home. Can I start today?
Staff
Of course. Fill out this form, and I will give you a key for a locker.
Narrator

questions.exp: She says she would like to join the gym.

questions.exp: The worker says twenty dollars a month.

o: To suggest a cheaper way to pay for classes
To say yoga is too difficult

parts.title: Astronomy Lecture: Why the Moon Has Phases
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in an astronomy class.
Professor

Today we will talk about the Moon. Have you ever noticed that the Moon changes shape during the month? Sometimes it is a full circle, and sometimes it is a thin curve. We call these changes the phases of the Moon.
Professor
Many people think the Earth's shadow causes the phases. This is not true. The real reason is simple. The Moon does not make its own light. It only reflects light from the Sun.
Professor
The Moon travels around the Earth, and one trip takes about twenty-nine days. As it moves, we see different parts of its bright side.
Professor
When the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun, the bright side faces away from us. We cannot see it. We call this the new moon.
Professor
About two weeks later, the Earth is between the Moon and the Sun. Now we see the whole bright side. This is the full moon.
Professor
Between these two, we see half of the Moon. These are called quarter moons. There are two of them in each month.
Professor
The phases were very important for ancient people. Before calendars were common, farmers used the Moon to count days. The word month even comes from the word moon.
Professor
Next week, we will learn about eclipses. An eclipse does involve the Earth's shadow, so please do not confuse it with the phases.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Narrator
Listen again to part of the lecture. Then answer the question.
Professor
Many people think the Earth's shadow causes the phases. This is not true.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the lecture?
questions.exp: The professor explains the phases of the Moon.

questions.q: What does the Moon do with sunlight?
questions.exp: The Moon reflects light from the Sun.

questions.q: About how long does the Moon take to travel around the Earth?
questions.exp: One trip takes about twenty-nine days.

questions.q: What do we see during a full moon?
questions.exp: The Earth is between the Moon and Sun, so we see the whole bright side.

questions.q: Why does the professor say this: "This is not true"?
questions.exp: He corrects the idea that Earth's shadow causes phases.

questions.q: How did ancient farmers use the Moon?
questions.exp: They used the Moon to count days before calendars.
